classification.difficultyReason: Uses separated circular groups and the resulting seating structure to determine a probability.

content.prompt: A sports committee consisting of four rowers, three basketballers and two cricketers sit at a circular table.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How many different arrangements of the committee are possible if the rowers and basketballers both sit together in groups, but no rower sits next to a basketballer?

answer.worked:
The cricketers must separate the rower and basketballer groups on both sides. Form the big unit RRRR C BBB and leave the other cricketer outside it. There are two choices for the cricketer inside this unit. The big unit and the remaining cricketer have $1!$ circular arrangement. Arrange the rowers in $4!$ ways and the basketballers in $3!$ ways.
$$\begin{aligned}N&=2\times1!\times4!\times3!\\&=288\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: One rower and one cricketer are related. If the conditions in part a apply, what is the probability that these two members of the committee will sit next to one another?

answer.worked:
The rowers are between the two cricketers in the sequence CRRRRC. The particular cricketer is adjacent to exactly one of the four rower positions. Each rower is equally likely to occupy that position.
$$P(\text{related pair adjacent})=\frac14.$$
